def repeated_name_value_total(names, values):
    """Tally the flagged returns at close of shift.

    Every evening the returns desk at Marlowe's General closes out with the
    same small headache. Customers bring items back all day long, and
    whichever clerk is on duty logs each one under the name printed on its
    tag, along with an adjustment value — sometimes a refund, sometimes a
    restocking charge, so the figure may well be negative. Head office, for
    its part, cares about only one slice of the ledger: the items that came
    back under a name appearing on the log more than once. A recurring name
    on the returns log is the desk's informal signal that a product line
    deserves a second look, and the accountants upstairs want to know the
    total money tied up in exactly those entries before the drawer is
    counted.

    The day's log reaches you as two parallel lists. names is a list of
    strings and values is a list of ints of the same length; names[i] and
    values[i] describe the same item. Your function performs the
    close-of-shift tally the accountants ask for. Return the sum of the
    values of the items whose name appears MORE THAN ONCE in names (0 if
    none repeats). The clerks will paste the resulting number into the
    nightly reconciliation sheet, sign the drawer over to the morning crew,
    and go home.

    >>> repeated_name_value_total([], [])
    0
    >>> repeated_name_value_total(['dyn', 'eel', 'cam', 'dyn', 'cam'], [16, -4, -2, 18, 30])
    62
    """
